subject: psychiatry
title: Cannabis, Cocaine, and Psychostimulant Misuse Syndromes

steps.tx: **Cannabis pharmacology** is driven by its primary psychoactive cannabinoid delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), which acts as a partial agonist at presynaptic CB1 receptors in the basal ganglia, cerebellum, and cerebral cortex. Acute intoxication characteristically causes bilateral conjunctival injection (ciliary flush), dry mouth, resting tachycardia, and intense hyperphagia.
steps.say: Cannabis THC activates central CB1 receptors, producing acute intoxication marked by conjunctival injection, dry mouth, tachycardia, and increased appetite.

vis.caption: Mesolimbic dopamine reward pathway activation and monoamine transporter blockade by psychostimulants.

steps.tx: **Amotivational syndrome** represents a chronic neurobehavioral disturbance developing in regular, heavy cannabis users, characterized by pervasive apathy, avolition, loss of ambition, and severe cognitive slowing. Sufferers become chronically indifferent to academic achievement, career advancement, and personal hygiene, displaying blunted emotional reactivity.
steps.say: Amotivational syndrome arises from heavy chronic cannabis use, causing persistent apathy, loss of ambition, and academic and social decline.

left.title: Amotivational Syndrome
points: Pervasive apathy and loss of personal drive
Dropping out of employment or university
Slow insidious onset with heavy cannabis use

steps.tx: **Cannabis-induced psychotic disorder** presents as an acute psychotic episode triggered by high-potency THC consumption, featuring prominent paranoid persecutory delusions, auditory hallucinations, depersonalisation, and acute panic. While symptoms typically resolve within days of cessation, adolescent exposure substantially increases lifetime vulnerability to developing chronic schizophrenia.
steps.say: Cannabis can trigger acute paranoia and auditory hallucinations. Heavy adolescent use significantly increases the lifetime risk of developing schizophrenia.

nodes.label: Adolescent cannabis exposure during active prefrontal pruning
Dysregulation of central endocannabinoid and dopaminergic pathways
Acute cannabis-induced psychotic decompensation with paranoia
Substantial permanent increase in schizophrenia transition risk

steps.tx: Look at the scratched, picked skin covering the arms in this picture. Cocaine can produce **Magnan sign**, a tactile hallucination in which imagined insects seem to crawl under the skin, driving relentless scratching and excoriation. Recognising that pattern helps clinicians ask about stimulant use in a patient presenting with formication, agitation, and skin lesions that cannot be explained by infestation or primary skin disease alone.
steps.say: Imagined insects crawling under the skin is Magnan sign, a cocaine effect. The resulting excoriations should prompt questions about stimulant use.

vis.alt: Clinical illustration of cocaine-induced tactile hallucinations, with skin excoriations from picking at imagined insects and the Magnan sign
vis.caption: Clinical illustration of cocaine-induced tactile hallucinations showing excoriation and the Magnan sign. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Cocaine mechanism of action** operates by binding to and blocking presynaptic monoamine reuptake transporters, specifically the dopamine transporter (DAT), noradrenaline transporter (NET), and serotonin transporter (SERT). The resultant massive accumulation of synaptic dopamine in the nucleus accumbens drives intense euphoria, hyper-alertness, grandiosity, and intense addiction.
steps.say: Cocaine blocks dopamine, noradrenaline, and serotonin reuptake transporters, flooding the nucleus accumbens to induce intense euphoria and addiction.

steps.tx: **Magnan sign and formication** describe a bizarre tactile hallucinatory phenomenon classically encountered in chronic cocaine intoxication and delirium. Patients experience vivid sensations of insects, parasites, or worms crawling across or beneath their skin ('cocaine bugs'), prompting frantic, excoriating scratching that produces extensive ulcerations and needle-like skin gouges.
steps.say: Magnan sign is a tactile hallucination in chronic cocaine use where patients feel bugs crawling under their skin, causing frantic scratching and ulcers.

vis.title: Tactile Hallucinations Compared
rows: Insects or lice crawling under cutaneous tissue
Small ants crawling across skin surface
Fixed non-bizarre belief of skin parasite infection
Unilateral tingling or electric shock sensations

steps.tx: **Cardiovascular complications of cocaine** stem from potent sympathomimetic stimulation combined with local anaesthetic blockade of cardiac voltage-gated sodium channels. Cocaine induces severe coronary artery vasoconstriction, accelerates platelet aggregation, and drastically increases myocardial oxygen demand, precipitating acute myocardial infarction even in young individuals.
steps.say: Cocaine causes coronary vasospasm, accelerated platelet thrombosis, and arrhythmias, precipitating acute myocardial infarction in young healthy individuals.

vis.title: Cocaine Cardiovascular Complications
rows: Vasospasm combined with acute platelet thrombosis
Intravenous nitroprusside or labetalol with caution
Blockade of cardiac sodium channels (Class I effect)

steps.tx: **Amphetamine psychosis** develops during binge consumption of methamphetamine or dextroamphetamine, presenting with persecutory delusions, auditory hallucinations, extreme paranoia, and aggressive agitation. Clinically identical to paranoid schizophrenia, it is driven by massive amphetamine-induced vesicular release and reverse transport of dopamine via DAT.
steps.say: Amphetamine psychosis mimics paranoid schizophrenia with delusions and auditory hallucinations, driven by massive reverse-transport release of dopamine.

left.title: Amphetamine Psychosis
points: Vesicular release and reverse DAT transport
Typically resolves within days of abstinence

right.title: Paranoid Schizophrenia
points: Affective blunting and formal thought disorder

steps.tx: **LSD flashbacks**, formally categorized as Hallucinogen Persisting Perception Disorder (HPPD), involve the spontaneous, distressing recurrence of perceptual distortions experienced during previous lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD) intoxication. Sufferers experience geometric visual hallucinations, false perceptions of movement in peripheral fields, flashes of color, and trailing images (palinopsia).
steps.say: LSD flashbacks involve recurrent visual disturbances like trailing images and halos months after drug use, designated hallucinogen persisting perception disorder.
